module_title: Magnetism, Fleming's Rules, and Electromagnetic Induction (EMI)
introduction: Electricity and Magnetism are two sides of the same coin. Flowing current can create a magnet (Motor), and a moving magnet can create current (Generator). This is the basis of global power generation.

core_concepts.title: Magnetic Effect of Electric Current
core_concepts.description:
Hans Christian Oersted discovered that a wire carrying electric current produces a 'Magnetic Field' around it. 
Right-Hand Thumb Rule: If your thumb points in the direction of the current, your curled fingers show the direction of the magnetic field lines.

core_concepts.title: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule (For Motors)
core_concepts.description:
Stretch the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of your left hand mutually perpendicular to each other: 
Forefinger = Magnetic Field 
Middle finger = Current 
Thumb = 'Direction of Force/Motion'. 
Application: The 'Electric Motor' works on this principle (converts Electrical energy into Mechanical energy).

core_concepts.title: Electromagnetic Induction (EMI)
core_concepts.description: Discovered by Michael Faraday: When there is relative motion between a coil and a magnet, the changing 'Magnetic Flux' induces an 'Induced Current' inside the coil.

core_concepts.title: Fleming's Right-Hand Rule (For Generators)
core_concepts.description:
This rule is used to find the direction of the 'Induced Current' when a conductor is moved in a magnetic field. 
Application: The 'Electric Generator (Dynamo)' works on EMI (converts Mechanical energy into Electrical energy).

important_entities.name: The Transformer
important_entities.significance: A device working on the principle of 'Mutual Induction'. It is used to Step-Up (increase) or Step-Down (decrease) AC voltages. Note: A transformer NEVER changes the 'Power' or the 'Frequency' of the current.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: 'Can a transformer be used to step up the voltage of a DC battery?' Answer: Absolutely NOT! Transformers require a constantly changing magnetic field to work, which only AC (Alternating Current) provides. Connecting it to DC will burn the primary coil.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Motor = M = Mains (Current in) = Left. Generator = G = Generate (Current out) = Right.
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: In a Motor, you put current IN (Mains). In a Generator, you get current OUT (Generate). Use Left hand for Motors to find force, use Right hand for Generators to find induced current.

exam_strategy_tips: Highly repeated in NDA/State PCS: 'What is the working principle of a Dynamo?' Answer: Electromagnetic Induction (EMI).
